subject: Runtime packaging, migration credits and pricing alignment for CloudForge evaluation
messages:
From: Michael Lang <m.lang@cloudforge.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cloudforge.com
Date: Tue, 08 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing parity ask + migration credit details

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudForge is excited about Redwood's latency and caching approach. Our procurement team has asked if you can match the per-token economics we're currently being quoted by EdgeRun (they're offering a blended $0.00095/token for 8k context models with a pilot credit).

Two follow-ups we need to clarify to move forward:
- Can Redwood match the blended per-token rate for a 6-month pilot?
- What migration/transition credits would you offer to offset egress and engineering uplift?
- Are there packaging differences (seats vs. consumption buckets) that affect the unit price once we exit pilot?

I've attached our simple TCO workbook; if you can send a compact counter-proposal (pricing + any onboarding credits) by EOD Thursday, procurement will escalate to signatures.

Attachments: cloudforge_tco_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

Best,
Michael
Michael Lang
Head of Platform Ops, CloudForge
m.lang@cloudforge.com

Michael —

Appreciate the clarity and the TCO. We can get a focused response, but need a short internal alignment first on what concessions we can provide without undermining our Dedicated capacity commitments. Looping in Marissa (commercial) and Olga (procurement/legal) to own the numbers and contract framing.

We should be able to put a firm pilot credit + a conditional migration credit tied to committed MRR after pilot. Can you confirm the pilot volume profile (tokens/day) and whether CloudForge needs a guaranteed SLA during pilot or if a best-effort hosted tier is sufficient?

I'll follow up with a compact proposal by Wed EOD.

Thanks,
Rafael

Date: Wed, 09 Jul 2025 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: preliminary counter and packaging options for CloudForge

Team —

Quick draft for Rafael to send to Michael; two packaging alternatives and the conditional credits. Please review edits inline.

Option A — Consumption-first (hosted)
- Blended pilot rate: $0.00092/token for pilot (up from our floor to be competitive).
- Pilot credit: $40k applied to invoices across first 60 days (reduces net pilot cost).
- Migration credit: Up to $75k credit if customer converts to a 12-month committed band >= $25k/mo within 90 days of pilot end. Credit applies as account-level invoice credits over first 3 months after conversion.
- Notes: No SLA upgrade for pilot; best-effort hosted included.

Option B — Dedicated-lite (reserved pool)
- Effective unit economics: $0.00085/token with a 12-month reservation (minimum commit $300k).
- Pilot credit: $25k (smaller, because conversion is presumed to be reservation).
- Migration credit: $50k payable as implementation service credit for on-prem/network egress work.
- Notes: Faster support SLA and onboarding concierge; recommended for lower-latency 24/7 workloads.

Commercial trade-offs to flag to CloudForge:
- Seat vs. consumption packaging: We typically keep runtime and token unit pricing separate from user-seat fees. Bundling seats can give accounting simplicity but rarely meaningfully reduces token unit price unless combined with a substantial commit.
- Egress/engineering uplift: we prefer credits applied to professional-services/integration line items rather than token-rate discounts (simpler to sunset).

Attachments suggested: redwood_runtime_packaging_v2.pdf (one-pager that contrasts both options), annotated TCO that maps their workbook to our offer.

If all ok, Rafael can send a short note with both options and request the pilot volume profile.

Olga
Director, Commercial Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Michael Lang <m.lang@cloudforge.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cloudforge.com
Date: Thu, 10 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + migration credit details

Olga / Rafael / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turn. Helpful framing. A few clarifications from procurement/engineering:
1) Pilot volume: expected ~12M tokens over 30 days (spiky, 80% read / 20% write)
2) We need the migration credit to cover estimated egress + setup (~$60k). If CloudForge signs the 12-month commit, we can do $30k/mo for 12 months in the committed band (we prefer consumption).
3) On the SLA: we need a 99.5% availability target during the pilot window for critical endpoints — can you add a pilot SLA addendum?

Also: can you confirm whether credits are taxable / whether they appear as negative invoice lines? Our accounting team requires a statement.

I'll share the internal TCO workbook edits tonight. If you can confirm the two points (pilot credit and SLA addendum) by EOD, procurement will move to contracting.

Best,
Michael

Subject: Re: Pricing parity ask + migration credit details

Michael —

Thanks for the volume and SLA info. We can do the following, final offer:
- Pilot: $0.00090/token with a $40k pilot credit applied as negative invoice line during first 60 days.
- Migration credit: $60k credit (applied as invoice credit) if CloudForge converts to a 12-month consumption commit >= $25k/mo within 90 days of pilot end.
- Pilot SLA: 99.5% for the pilot endpoints; addendum will be attached to the pilot SOW.
- Credits are invoiced as negative line items (tax treatment follows local tax rules; we'll include language in the SOW saying credits appear as invoice adjustments — procurement should run this by accounting).

We will also include a one-page packaging appendix that maps the seat/consumption trade-offs and shows the net monthly run-rate at their stated 12M token pace. I'm attaching the one-pager and a redlined pilot SOW.

Attachments: redwood_runtime_packaging_v2.pdf (one-pager), pilot_sow_redline.docx (contract redline)

If this works, Rafael — please propose a short 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize wording and get DocuSign started.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Deals, Redwood Inference
